nodes.summary: The run decomposition of a Boolean word is the list, from left to right, of its maximal runs of equal consecutive letters, each recorded as the pair (letter, length of the run).
nodes.title: Maximal runs of a Boolean word

nodes.summary: Let $r = 3$ and $s = 2$. The set $Q_4^{3/2}$ of $Q$-bonacci paths of semilength $4$, that is, the Dyck paths of semilength $4$ and height at most $2$ whose block word's maximal runs satisfy the $Q$-bonacci run condition, has $7$ elements, while the set $\tilde R_5^{3/2}$ of Dyck paths of semilength $5$ and height at most $2$ whose block word's maximal runs satisfy the rational run condition has $6$ elements.
nodes.title: Path counts for $q = 3/2$

nodes.summary: For a Dyck word $P = P_0 P_1 \cdots P_{2n-1}$ of semilength $n$, with steps indexed from $0$, the block word of $P$ is the Boolean word of length $n - 1$ (empty when $n = 0$) whose entry $i$, for $0 \le i < n - 1$, is true exactly when $P_{2i+1} = U$.
nodes.title: Block word of a Dyck path of height at most $2$

nodes.title: $Q$-bonacci and rational-run paths correspond exactly when $s \equiv 1 \pmod r$

nodes.summary: A Dyck word has height at most $2$ when no prefix of it has more than two more up steps $U$ than down steps $D$.
nodes.title: Dyck words of height at most $2$

nodes.summary: Writing $1$ for true and $0$ for false, for $r = 4$ and $s = 5$ the maximal runs of the Boolean word $1001100$ do not satisfy the $Q$-bonacci run condition, while the maximal runs of $100111100$ and of $100111$ do.

For the run at position $i$, let $v_i$ be the length of the run at position $i + 1$ if that run exists and has letter false, and $v_i = 0$ otherwise. nodes.title: The $Q$-bonacci run condition

nodes.summary: Let $r, s \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $R$ be a list of runs, each a pair (letter, length) with a Boolean letter. For the run at position $i$, let $v_i$ be the length of the run at position $i + 1$ if that run exists and has letter false, and $v_i = 0$ otherwise. Then $R$ satisfies the rational run condition for $q = r/s$ when every run of letter true, say of length $p$ at position $i$, has $p \le r$ and $p s \le r v_i$.
nodes.title: The rational Dyck path run condition

nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 1$ and $t$ be natural numbers and $s = t r + 1$. Then for every $n \ge 0$ the set $Q_n^{r/s}$ of $Q$-bonacci paths of semilength $n$ is in bijection with the set $\tilde R_{n+t+1}^{r/s}$ of Dyck paths of semilength $n + t + 1$ and height at most $2$ whose block word's maximal runs satisfy the rational run condition for $q = r/s$.
nodes.title: $Q$-bonacci and rational-run paths are in bijection when $s = t r + 1$

nodes.title: The $Q$-bonacci paths $Q_n^{r/s}$

nodes.summary: Let $R = ((b_0, m_0), \dots, (b_{k-1}, m_{k-1}))$ be a list of pairs of a Boolean letter and a natural number, read as the maximal runs of a block word in which the letter $\mathrm{false}$ stands for a $0$-valley $DU$. For $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of $0$-valleys immediately after run $i$ is $m_{i+1}$ if $i + 1 < k$ and $b_{i+1} = \mathrm{false}$, and $0$ otherwise.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
